children.value: This appendix lists the primary online resources for macroeconomic research, organized by function: data retrieval, model solving, research access, and professional development.
FRED API (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

children.label: FRED API (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

children.value: Free, registration required for API key.
The FRED API provides programmatic access to over 800,000 economic time series. A basic call in Python:

from fredapi import Fred
fred = Fred(api_key='your_key')
gdp = fred.get_series('GDPC1')  # Real GDP, seasonally adjusted

Provides WEO, BOP, IFS (International Financial Statistics), and other IMF databases via JSON API. The
Access to OECD databases including Economic Outlook, Main Economic Indicators, and structural indicators.
Free download (bulk) or query via API.
Provides credit, property prices, effective exchange rates, and international banking statistics.
The dominant language for empirical economics. Key packages:
: Dynamic linear models with time-series support.
: Vector autoregression estimation, Granger causality, impulse responses.
: Comprehensive unit root and cointegration testing (Johansen test).
: Applied Econometrics with R — IV, 2SLS, hypothesis tests.
: Panel data models (fixed/random effects, Hausman test).
Data science, DSGE model solving, machine learning applications.
: OLS, IV, time-series models (VAR, ARIMA, state-space).
: Tools from Ljungqvist and Sargent; dynamic programming, Markov chains.
Traditional platform for DSGE model solving. The
toolbox (below) runs on MATLAB and Octave and is the standard for DSGE estimation.
Free, open source (works with MATLAB or Octave).
Dynare is the standard tool for solving and estimating DSGE models. Given a

file specifying model equations, it: (i) linearizes around the steady state; (ii) solves the linear rational expectations model; (iii) computes impulse response functions; (iv) estimates parameters by MLE or Bayesian MCMC; (v) conducts model comparison. Used by central banks worldwide.
Less common in pure macro than R or Python but standard in empirical work drawing on microeconomic data (household surveys, firm-level data). Key commands:
K.3 DSGE Model Databases and Replication Archives

children.label: K.3 DSGE Model Databases and Replication Archives

children.value: A collection of 100+ published DSGE models in a common Dynare framework, enabling systematic comparison of model properties and impulse responses across models.
Working papers from European macroeconomists. Subscription required for full access (many universities have access).
The primary archive for U.S.-based macroeconomic research. Papers are freely available to the public after an embargo period.

The American Economic Review and associated journals require authors to post data and code for replication. The replication archives contain the datasets and code for most published empirical papers in these journals.
Preprint server for economics and other social sciences. Most working papers are freely available here before (and after) publication.
K.4 Central Bank Research and Publications

children.label: K.4 Central Bank Research and Publications

children.value: : Semi-annual to Congress, with current economic assessment.
: Qualitative regional economic conditions, released 8× per year.
Each regional Fed bank publishes research and commentary:
: Accessible commentary from NY Fed economists.
: Focus on banking and financial stability.
: Focus on West Coast economy, international macroeconomics.
: Strong research tradition in monetary economics.
: Bi-weekly assessment of euro area conditions.
: Accessible commentary for a broader audience.
: Research on monetary policy, financial stability.
: Financial market commentary and statistical tables.
: Comprehensive annual assessment of global economy.
: Large archive of IMF staff research.
: Accessible commentary on current economic issues.

Open-source lectures on quantitative economics (Python and Julia). Written by Thomas Sargent and John Stachurski. Covers dynamic programming, search models, asset pricing, Markov chains, and linear rational expectations models at graduate level.

Many sessions post lecture slides and videos. Particularly valuable: Macroeconomics and Productivity, International Finance and Macroeconomics, Monetary Economics, and Economic Fluctuations and Growth.
Annual intensive courses at the ASSA meetings in January. Recent topics have included machine learning in economics, empirical bayes methods, and identification in structural models.
The Economics of Climate Change (Yale Climate Economics)

children.label: The Economics of Climate Change (Yale Climate Economics)

children.value: Resources on integrated assessment modeling, DICE/RICE models, and climate-economy linkages.
Accessible, carefully constructed visualizations of long-run global economic, social, and environmental data. Useful for communicating macroeconomic trends to non-specialist audiences.
Professional financial news sources with real-time data. Bloomberg Terminal provides the most comprehensive real-time financial data but is expensive; the Bloomberg Economics portal (
economics coverage and graphics are consistently high quality.
publishes short commentaries by leading economists on current policy questions.
